intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently for an authentic culinary adventure.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Street Food
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, famous for its colorful silk lanterns, French colonial architecture, and vibrant street food scene. Try Cao Lau noodles and White Rose dumplings at the bustling night market, and release a lantern on the Thu Bon River for a magical cultural experience.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic mountain roads stretching between Da Nang and Hue. Enjoy breathtaking coastal views, stop at old war bunkers, and experience the freedom of backpacker travel in Vietnam at its finest.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Boat Tour & Local Village Visit
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, cruising narrow waterways by wooden boat through lush rice paddies and floating markets. Visit local villages, sample tropical fruits, watch traditional coconut candy being made, and gain deep insight into rural Vietnamese life and culture.

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Nightlife & Backpacker Scene
experiences.description: Dive into the heart of Ho Chi Minh City's legendary backpacker district on Bui Vien Street. Enjoy cheap local beers, sizzling street food stalls, live music, and a vibrant international atmosphere. This is the ultimate hub for budget travelers to connect, swap travel tips, and experience Vietnam's energetic urban nightlife.
experiences.location: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the 86 airport bus (~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a slow walk around Hoan Kiem Lake to shake off jet lag. Admire Ngoc Son Temple on the lake and soak in the vibrant street energy.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Old Quarter's 36 ancient streets on foot. Visit the famous Dong Xuan Market for a taste of local commerce. Join the weekend walking street if arriving on a weekend evening.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a Banh Mi from a street cart near the airport or Old Quarter (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Cha at Bun Cha Huong Lien (famous spot in Old Quarter) - ~60,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a gold shop in the Old Quarter for better rates. Avoid taxi touts - use Grab app for affordable and reliable rides. SIM card available at airport for ~150,000 VND.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (free, opens 7:30 AM - check schedule as it closes periodically). Walk through Ba Dinh Square and admire the Presidential Palace exterior. Visit the One Pillar Pagoda nearby (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entry) - one of Southeast Asia's best cultural museums showcasing 54 ethnic groups. Spend 2–3 hours exploring indoor and outdoor exhibits. Return to Old Quarter by local bus (~7,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Old Quarter night scene. Visit Bia Hoi Corner (Hang Buom & Luong Ngoc Quyen intersection) for the world's cheapest draft beer (~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) and meet fellow backpackers.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at a local street stall near the hotel (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a street vendor near the museum (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Rieu (crab noodle soup) from a street cart in the Old Quarter (~40,000 VND) + Bia Hoi

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for the Mausoleum visit (no shorts or sleeveless tops). The Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays for maintenance. Arrive early to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hoa Lo Prison Museum ('Hanoi Hilton') (~30,000 VND) - a sobering and historically rich site. Then walk to St. Joseph's Cathedral (free) in the French Quarter for architecture and atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) (~30,000 VND) - Vietnam's first university dating to 1070. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the beautiful courtyards and pavilions. Walk or take a Grab to the Fine Arts Museum (~40,000 VND) for Vietnamese art spanning centuries.
day_by_day.evening: Watch a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (~100,000 VND) - a uniquely Vietnamese art form. Afterward, browse the night market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri–Sun evenings).

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean) from a street vendor (~20,000–25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Binh Dan (local rice plate with multiple dishes) near Temple of Literature (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Nem Cuon (fresh spring rolls) + Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish) at a local restaurant (~80,000–100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book Water Puppet Show tickets in advance or arrive 30 minutes early. The show runs about 50 minutes and is excellent value for the cultural experience.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18 (Day Trip to Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat station to Ninh Binh (~2 hours, ~80,000–100,000 VND). Rent a bicycle upon arrival (~50,000 VND/day) and cycle to Trang An Landscape Complex. Take a boat tour through the limestone karst caves and rice paddies (~200,000 VND, 2–3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free) built into a limestone cliff. Climb to the upper cave for panoramic views over the valley. Continue to Mua Cave viewpoint (~100,000 VND) and hike 500 steps to the dragon statue for breathtaking views of Tam Coc.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus. Rest and enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or street snack before departing Hanoi (~20,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Ga (chicken rice) at a local eatery in Ninh Binh town (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Pho or Bun Bo Nam Bo back in Hanoi Old Quarter (~40,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: This is a full day trip - depart by 7:00–7:30 AM. Ninh Binh is often called 'Ha Long Bay on land.' Bring sunscreen and water. The last bus back to Hanoi typically departs around 17:00–18:00.

day_by_day.morning: Check out from Hanoi hotel. Take a Grab to Hanoi train station. Board the Reunification Express train to Hue (~14 hours overnight or opt for a 12-hour day train). Book a soft seat (~200,000–350,000 VND) for comfort. Enjoy the scenic countryside views from the train.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle in on the train. The journey passes through beautiful rural Vietnamese landscapes, mountains, and coastline. Chat with locals and fellow travelers.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hue in the evening (if taking a fast train) or overnight (sleeper train). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Hue (~100,000–150,000 VND/night). Explore the area around Pham Ngu Lao Street.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Xoi from a street vendor near Hanoi station (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Train snacks or packed lunch - buy cup noodles or snacks at the station (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup, a Hue specialty) at a local restaurant upon arrival (~40,000–50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance at baolau.com or the station. The train ride itself is a scenic backpacker experience. Bring a light jacket as train AC can be cold. Overnight sleeper trains save on accommodation costs.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~100,000–150,000 VND/day) and explore the Imperial Citadel of Hue (~200,000 VND entry) - a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Forbidden Purple City, gates, and pavilions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Tombs - Minh Mang Tomb and Tu Duc Tomb (~100,000 VND each or combo ticket). These are some of Vietnam's most atmospheric historical sites set in forested hillside grounds. Take a dragon boat on the Perfume River (~150,000 VND) for scenic views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River at sunset. Visit Dong Ba Market for local crafts and street food. Try Hue's famous street food scene around Truong Dinh Street.

meals.breakfast: Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancake) at a street stall (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) - a Hue specialty (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Beo (steamed rice cakes), Banh Nam, and Banh Loc at a local Hue restaurant (~50,000–80,000 VND for a spread)

day_by_day.notes: Hue is known for its refined royal cuisine - don't miss the unique local dishes. The city is very bikeable and flat. Respect dress codes at the Citadel (no shorts or sleeveless tops).

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - April 21 (Hue to Hoi An via Hai Van Pass)
day_by_day.morning: Hire a motorbike taxi or join a group tour to travel the scenic Hai Van Pass (~200,000–300,000 VND) from Hue to Da Nang. Stop at the top of the pass for stunning ocean and mountain views. This is one of Vietnam's most iconic road journeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop briefly in Da Nang (optional: visit Dragon Bridge or My Khe Beach). Continue by local bus or minivan to Hoi An (~1 hour from Da Nang, ~50,000 VND). Check in to a budget guesthouse in or near the Ancient Town (~120,000–180,000 VND/night).
day_by_day.evening: Walk through Hoi An Ancient Town (free to walk around, ~120,000 VND for entry to 5 heritage sites). Admire the lantern-lit streets, Japanese Covered Bridge, and merchant houses. Watch lanterns float on the Thu Bon River.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart in Hue before departure (~20,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Mi Quang (Quang noodles) at a roadside stop or in Da Nang (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cao Lau (Hoi An specialty noodles) at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass is breathtaking but can be foggy - the views are still spectacular. This route was famously featured on Top Gear. Book accommodation in Hoi An in advance as it's a popular backpacker destination.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND/day) and cycle to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (~5 km from town). Spend the morning swimming and relaxing on the beach. Return to town by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ancient Town's heritage sites with your ticket - visit the Japanese Covered Bridge, Tan Ky Old House, Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and the Museum of Trading Ceramics. Browse the vibrant Central Market for local produce and street food.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class (budget options from ~250,000–350,000 VND) that includes a market tour and hands-on cooking of Vietnamese dishes. Alternatively, join a lantern-making workshop (~100,000–150,000 VND).

meals.breakfast: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) - a Hoi An exclusive (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh Mi Phuong - arguably Vietnam's most famous Banh Mi (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at a local eatery (~45,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Ancient Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. Tailors in Hoi An offer custom clothing at reasonable prices if interested. Avoid peak afternoon heat by resting during 12:00–14:00.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Check out from Hoi An guesthouse. Take a shuttle bus to Da Nang Airport (~100,000–150,000 VND). Fly from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (~1 hour, budget airlines like VietJet or Bamboo from ~400,000–800,000 VND if booked in advance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Take bus 109 from Tan Son Nhat Airport to central Saigon (~20,000 VND) or Grab (~100,000–150,000 VND). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district (~120,000–180,000 VND/night). Explore the lively backpacker street.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Bui Vien Walking Street - the famous backpacker nightlife hub. Experience the sensory overload of neon lights, street food, and live music. Try local draft beer and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or light snack before heading to the airport (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport food or snacks on the plane (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh noodle soup) at a street stall in Pham Ngu Lao (~40,000–50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Da Nang to HCMC flight well in advance for the best budget fares. Alternatively, take an overnight sleeper bus (~200,000–300,000 VND) to save on accommodation. Pham Ngu Lao is the backpacker hub with the most budget options.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) - one of Vietnam's most powerful and important museums documenting the Vietnam War. Allow 2 hours. Walk to the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) and explore the historic building where the war officially ended in 1975.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica (free, exterior) and the Central Post Office (free) - a beautiful French colonial building still in operation. Explore Ben Thanh Market for souvenirs and street food. Walk through District 1 and admire the French colonial architecture along Dong Khoi Street.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Vietnam - splurge slightly on a rooftop restaurant or enjoy a farewell street food crawl through Pham Ngu Lao. Visit a local cafe for Vietnamese iced coffee (Ca Phe Sua Da) as a final taste of Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (egg Banh Mi) from a street cart (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) - a Saigon classic (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Lau (Vietnamese hot pot) shared with fellow travelers at a local restaurant (~80,000–120,000 VND per person) or a street food crawl (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally heavy - allow time to process. If time permits, consider a half-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~120,000 VND entry + ~150,000 VND transport) - an extraordinary underground wartime network. Pack souvenirs from Ben Thanh Market with bargaining expected.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a taxi or Grab car (~45 min, ~250,000 VND) to your boutique hotel in the Old Quarter. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle stroll through the 36 Ancient Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the iconic Dong Xuan Market. Pick up a Vietnamese coffee at a sidewalk café and soak in the chaotic, charming energy of Hanoi.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for the evening atmosphere — watch locals exercise and socialize around the lake. Visit Ngoc Son Temple (Jade Mountain Temple) if still open. Then explore the Old Quarter Night Market on Hang Dao Street for street food and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Skipped due to midday arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a bowl of Bun Cha (grilled pork noodles) at a local eatery near the Old Quarter — try Bun Cha Huong Lien (~80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl at the Old Quarter Night Market: Banh Mi, grilled skewers, and fresh spring rolls (~100,000–150,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a local gold shop in the Old Quarter for better rates. Get a local SIM card (Viettel or Vietnamobile) at the airport for ~150,000 VND with data.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a traditional Pho breakfast at a local spot near the hotel. Then visit Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son Temple in the calm morning hours (open 8:00–17:00, ~30,000 VND). Walk across The Huc Bridge and enjoy the peaceful lake scenery before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first national university, a stunning example of traditional Vietnamese architecture (~30,000 VND). Afterward, explore the nearby Fine Arts Museum of Vietnam for a deeper look at Vietnamese art history (~40,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre near Hoan Kiem Lake (~100,000 VND, book ahead). Afterward, wander Ta Hien Street — known as 'Beer Street' — for a bia hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND/glass) and local snacks.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street (~60,000 VND) — arrive early, lines form quickly
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodles) at a local restaurant near the Temple of Literature (~70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish with dill) — a Hanoi specialty — at Cha Ca Thang Long (~180,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Water Puppet Show in advance online or at the box office in the morning. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 5–7 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hoa Lo Prison (Hanoi Hilton) for a sobering and historically rich experience (~30,000 VND). Then walk to St. Joseph's Cathedral — a stunning French Gothic-style church in the heart of the Old Quarter, free to enter during opening hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND) — one of Southeast Asia's best ethnographic museums, showcasing 54 ethnic groups. Take a Grab car (~50,000 VND, ~15 min from Old Quarter). Spend 2–3 hours exploring indoor and outdoor exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter and take a cyclo (pedicab) ride through the narrow ancient streets for a classic Hanoi experience (~100,000–150,000 VND for 30 min, negotiate first). End the night at a rooftop bar on Luong Ngoc Quyen Street for city views.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a street stall near the hotel (~40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Oc (snail noodle soup) at a local Old Quarter eatery (~60,000 VND) — adventurous and authentic
meals.dinner: Set dinner at a mid-range Vietnamese restaurant in the Old Quarter such as Quan An Ngon (~200,000–250,000 VND per person) — great variety of regional dishes

day_by_day.notes: The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology is closed on Mondays. If visiting on a Monday, substitute with the Vietnam National Museum of History near Hoan Kiem (~40,000 VND).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi early by sleeper bus or train to Ninh Binh (~2 hours, ~100,000–150,000 VND). Check in to a guesthouse in Tam Coc or Trang An area. Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and cycle through the stunning karst limestone countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a traditional rowing boat tour through Trang An Landscape Complex (UNESCO World Heritage Site, ~200,000 VND, ~3 hours). Glide through caves, rice paddies, and towering limestone cliffs. Alternatively, visit Tam Coc for a similar but shorter boat experience.
day_by_day.evening: Climb up to Hang Mua Peak (Dragon Mountain) for a panoramic sunset view over the rice fields and karst mountains (~100,000 VND). The 500-step climb is rewarding — arrive 1 hour before sunset for the best light.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street cart near the hotel in Hanoi before departure (~30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (rice plate with sides) near Tam Coc (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Grilled goat meat (de nui) — Ninh Binh's regional specialty — at a local restaurant in Tam Coc village (~150,000–200,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh is a popular day trip but staying overnight gives you access to early morning mist over the rice fields — magical for photography. Book accommodation in Tam Coc area for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for misty morning cycling through Tam Coc rice paddies — one of Vietnam's most iconic landscapes. Visit Bich Dong Pagoda (~10,000 VND), a beautiful cave pagoda built into the limestone cliffs, reachable by bicycle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Hue by train or sleeper bus (~5–6 hours, ~200,000–300,000 VND). The journey passes through beautiful coastal scenery. Check in to a guesthouse near Hue's Imperial City. Rest and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening walk along the Perfume River (Song Huong). Visit Dong Ba Market for an authentic local shopping and street food experience. Explore the vibrant Pham Ngu Lao Street area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Banh Mi from a street stall near your Ninh Binh guesthouse (~40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at a train station stop — rice boxes sold on Vietnamese trains (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodles) at a local restaurant in Hue (~60,000–80,000 VND) — the authentic version is far better than elsewhere

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets from Ninh Binh to Hue in advance via the Vietnam Railways app or 12go.asia. The SE trains are more comfortable than local trains.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Dai Noi) — the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty (~150,000 VND). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Forbidden Purple City, royal gates, and imperial gardens. Hire a local guide for ~100,000 VND extra for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~100,000–150,000 VND/day) and ride the Royal Tomb Trail. Visit Tu Duc Tomb (~150,000 VND) — the most elaborate and scenic of the Nguyen emperor tombs — set among pine forests and lotus ponds.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a Royal Hue Cuisine dinner — a unique culinary tradition featuring many small, beautifully presented dishes. Then stroll across Truong Tien Bridge at night for lovely river views illuminated by colorful lights.

meals.breakfast: Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancakes with shrimp and pork) at a local eatery (~50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) — a Hue specialty — at a street stall near Dong Ba Market (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Set royal cuisine dinner at Tinh Gia Vien or a similar mid-range restaurant (~200,000–300,000 VND per person) — a unique cultural dining experience

day_by_day.notes: April in Hue can be hot and occasionally rainy. Carry a light rain jacket. The Imperial Citadel requires modest dress — cover shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic bus or motorbike ride over Hai Van Pass (Cloud Pass) — one of Vietnam's most dramatic mountain roads with sweeping ocean views. Stop at the old French/American bunker at the summit for photos. Total journey to Hoi An: ~3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An and check in to a guesthouse near the Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot: visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, Tan Ky Old House (~80,000 VND), and the colorful lantern-lined streets.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hoi An's famous lantern-lit evening atmosphere — the Ancient Town glows beautifully after dark. Browse the Night Market on An Hoi Island. Try your hand at a lantern-making workshop (~150,000 VND, ~1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart in Hue before departure (~30,000 VND) — Hue has excellent Banh Mi too
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at Thanh Cao Lau restaurant (~70,000 VND) — only authentic in Hoi An
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Hoi An specialties at a riverside restaurant on Bach Dang Street (~150,000–200,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass is best experienced by motorbike for the full effect — Easy Rider tours from Hue (~400,000–600,000 VND) are a popular and safe option. Alternatively, the open-top bus from Da Nang passes over it.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND/day) and cycle to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (~5 km from Ancient Town). Enjoy a relaxed morning swimming and sunbathing on the relatively uncrowded shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the My Son Sanctuary (Hindu Cham temple ruins, UNESCO World Heritage Site, ~150,000 VND, ~45 min from Hoi An by motorbike or organized tour ~200,000 VND). Explore the ancient brick towers dating back to the 4th–14th centuries.
day_by_day.evening: Take a Hoi An Cooking Class (~400,000–600,000 VND, 3 hours including market visit) — learn to make Cao Lau, fresh spring rolls, and other local dishes. Many schools operate evening sessions. End with eating your own creations.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — arguably Vietnam's most famous Banh Mi (~35,000 VND) — arrive early to avoid the queue
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beachside shack at An Bang Beach (~150,000–200,000 VND for grilled fish, prawns, and beer)
meals.dinner: Eat the dishes you cooked in your cooking class, or grab Mi Quang (turmeric noodles) at a local street stall (~60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance — Hoi An has many options (Red Bridge, Morning Glory, and Thuan Tinh Island are well-regarded). My Son is best visited in the morning to avoid heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or take a sleeper bus to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Flight from Da Nang (~1 hour, ~800,000–1,200,000 VND with VietJet or Bamboo Airways) is recommended for time efficiency. Check in to a guesthouse in District 1 (Bui Vien or Pham Ngu Lao area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the heart of Saigon: visit the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND), the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — powerful and sobering — and the historic Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica and Central Post Office (free) — all within walking distance.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Bui Vien Walking Street — Saigon's famous backpacker strip — for street food, live music, and vibrant nightlife. Try a cold Saigon beer and mingle with travelers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Grab airport food or a quick Banh Mi in Hoi An before heading to Da Nang airport (~35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) at a local eatery in District 1 (~70,000–90,000 VND) — the quintessential Saigon lunch
meals.dinner: Street food on Bui Vien: Banh Trang Nuong (Vietnamese pizza), grilled skewers, and fresh coconut (~100,000–150,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense — allow time to process. Book your Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City flight in advance for the best prices. Download Grab app for affordable and reliable transport in Saigon.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~70 km from Saigon, ~150,000 VND entry + ~300,000–400,000 VND for organized tour or Grab). Explore the 250 km network of underground tunnels used by Viet Cong guerrillas — crawl through narrow passages and learn about wartime life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Saigon by early afternoon. Visit Ben Thanh Market for last-minute souvenir shopping and street food. Explore the trendy Nguyen Hue Walking Street and the HCMC Museum of History (~30,000 VND) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in District 1 for panoramic Saigon skyline views. Spend your last evening strolling along the Saigon River waterfront promenade, reflecting on 10 days of incredible Vietnamese experiences.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Hu Tieu (Southern-style noodle soup) at a local breakfast spot in District 1 (~60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh Mi and fresh sugarcane juice from a street cart near Ben Thanh Market (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Nha Hang Ngon (a beloved Saigon institution for Vietnamese cuisine) or a rooftop restaurant on Bui Vien (~200,000–300,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels tours depart from District 1 around 7:30–8:00 AM — book through your guesthouse or online the night before. If departing on a late-night or next-day flight, store luggage at your hotel and enjoy a final evening stroll. Vietnam has been an incredible journey — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, Hanoi (approx. 45–60 min). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your boutique room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore the narrow labyrinthine lanes of Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and Hang Ma (Paper Street). Visit Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake for a serene cultural introduction – watch the famous Huc Bridge reflect on the jade-green water.
day_by_day.evening: Evening cyclo ride through the illuminated Old Quarter streets for a cinematic first impression of Hanoi at night. Conclude at the vibrant Hoan Kiem Lake promenade for a leisurely walk.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack at hotel upon arrival or a quick stop at Banh Mi 25 (25 Hang Ca) – renowned artisan banh mi with premium fillings, a beloved Old Quarter institution.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Badiane (10 Nam Ngu St) – a celebrated French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant set in a stunning colonial villa. Try the tasting menu featuring locally sourced ingredients with refined French technique. Pair with a curated Vietnamese wine or cocktail.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the afternoon arrival. Ensure hotel arranges a private airport transfer. Confirm hotel concierge has itinerary pre-loaded for the following days.

day_by_day.morning: Premium guided cultural tour of the Hoan Kiem Lake district. Visit the Ngoc Son Temple in depth with a private guide explaining its Taoist and Confucian significance. Walk to St. Joseph's Cathedral (Nha Tho Lon) – a stunning neo-Gothic landmark. Explore the nearby Women's Museum or Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (pre-book private guided session).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class at a premium culinary school such as Hanoi Cooking Centre or Hidden Hanoi. Learn to prepare iconic northern Vietnamese dishes: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup), Bun Cha, and Nem Ran (spring rolls) with a market tour of Dong Xuan Market included.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (book premium front-row seats in advance). This 1,000-year-old art form is quintessentially Hanoian. Post-show, explore the atmospheric Ta Hien Street (Beer Street) for a curated street food walk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel or Cafe Giang (39 Nguyen Huu Huan) – birthplace of the legendary Egg Coffee (Ca Phe Trung). A must-have Hanoi experience.
meals.lunch: Lunch included in cooking class – enjoy the dishes you prepared.
meals.dinner: Street food premium tasting walk on Ta Hien and surrounding streets – curated stops include Bun Cha Huong Lien (the Obama Bun Cha spot), Banh Cuon Thanh Van, and Kem Trang Tien ice cream. Guided by a local food expert.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Water Puppet Theatre front-row seats at least 2 days in advance. The cooking class market tour starts early afternoon – confirm timing with the school.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (open mornings only, closed Mondays and Fridays). Includes the Presidential Palace gardens, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house, and the serene One Pillar Pagoda. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees required).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Fine Arts (66 Nguyen Thai Hoc) with a private art historian guide – discover lacquerware, silk paintings, and revolutionary art spanning centuries. Afterward, browse premium silk and lacquerware galleries on Hang Gai Street for curated souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Twilight Sky Bar (Rooftop, Hotel Nikko Hanoi) or Summit Lounge at Pan Pacific Hanoi – panoramic views of Hanoi's skyline and West Lake at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Pho Gia Truyen (49 Bat Dan) – the most iconic Pho Bo in Hanoi, a legendary hole-in-the-wall open since 1955. Arrive early to avoid queues.
meals.lunch: Lunch at KOTO (59 Van Mieu) – a social enterprise restaurant opposite the Temple of Literature, serving refined Vietnamese cuisine. Excellent Bun Cha and fresh rolls.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cha Ca La Vong (14 Cha Ca St) – Hanoi's most legendary restaurant, serving its singular dish: sizzling turmeric-marinated catfish cooked tableside with dill and spring onions, served over vermicelli. A 150-year-old institution.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays – verify the day before. Mausoleum visits are typically 7:30–10:30 AM only. Dress code strictly enforced.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium excursion to Halong Bay. Depart Hanoi by private luxury vehicle (approx. 3.5 hours). Board a premium overnight junk cruise – recommended vessels: Indochine Cruise, Paradise Elegance, or Au Co Cruise. Morning on the road with scenic countryside views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Halong Bay and embark on your luxury cruise. Afternoon kayaking through hidden lagoons and caves (Thien Cung Cave or Sung Sot Cave). Swim in emerald waters in a secluded cove. Sunset Tai Chi session on the sundeck.
day_by_day.evening: Gourmet seafood dinner onboard the cruise ship – freshly caught squid, prawns, and fish prepared by the ship's chef. Stargazing from the deck over the UNESCO World Heritage karst seascape. Optional squid fishing activity after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before 7:00 AM departure – hotel can arrange an early continental spread.
meals.lunch: Lunch served onboard the cruise upon embarkation – typically a lavish Vietnamese seafood spread.
meals.dinner: Premium multi-course seafood dinner onboard the cruise – fresh catch of the day, Halong Bay specialties including mantis shrimp, sea urchin, and grilled clams with lemongrass.

day_by_day.notes: Book the luxury cruise at least 2–3 weeks in advance. Bring motion sickness medication if sensitive. Pack light for the overnight – leave main luggage securely at Hanoi hotel. Confirm private transfer to Halong Bay pier.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise yoga or Tai Chi on the cruise sundeck. Kayak or bamboo boat tour through the floating fishing village of Cua Van – one of Vietnam's most photogenic communities. Visit a pearl farm for a demonstration of pearl cultivation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return cruise to Halong Bay pier. Private luxury transfer back to Hanoi (3.5 hours). Check back into Old Quarter hotel. Rest and refresh. Optional: visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) – Vietnam's first national university, founded in 1070.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hanoian night scene: visit the weekend Night Market on Hang Dao Street (if applicable) or browse artisan galleries on Nha Tho Street near St. Joseph's Cathedral.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast served onboard the cruise – Vietnamese and Western options with fresh tropical fruit and Pho.
meals.lunch: Lunch onboard before disembarkation – light Vietnamese fare.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Maison Van (Van Mieu area) or Green Tangerine (48 Hang Be) – a charming French-Vietnamese restaurant in a restored 1928 colonial house in the Old Quarter. Try the pan-seared duck breast with tamarind glaze.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transfer timing with cruise operator. Allow buffer time for traffic between Halong Bay pier and Hanoi. Temple of Literature closes at 5:30 PM – plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Morning flight from Hanoi (Noi Bai) to Hoi An via Da Nang (approx. 1.5 hours – Vietnam Airlines or Bamboo Airways business class). Private luxury transfer from Da Nang Airport to Hoi An Ancient Town (approx. 30 min). Check into a premium boutique hotel in or near Hoi An Ancient Town (e.g., Anantara Hoi An Resort or La Siesta Hoi An).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of Hoi An Ancient Town – a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Lai Vien Kieu), Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and the atmospheric merchant houses of Tran Phu Street. Explore the vibrant Central Market along the Thu Bon River.
day_by_day.evening: Hoi An Ancient Town transforms at night with hundreds of colorful silk lanterns illuminating the streets. Join a lantern-making workshop at a local artisan studio. Release a lotus lantern on the Thu Bon River for good luck.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel in Hanoi before airport transfer.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Banh Mi Phuong (2B Phan Chau Trinh) – Anthony Bourdain's declared 'best banh mi in the world.' A Hoi An institution.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Field Restaurant (Hoi An) – set in a stunning rice paddy field with open-air pavilions. Tasting menu of refined Central Vietnamese cuisine featuring cao lau, white rose dumplings, and grilled fish in banana leaf.

day_by_day.notes: Book business class flights in advance for comfort. Confirm hotel in Hoi An is pre-arranged before departure. The Ancient Town is best explored on foot – wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Private bicycle tour through the lush Hoi An countryside – cycle through rice paddies, vegetable farms, and traditional villages. Visit Tra Que Vegetable Village, a 400-year-old organic farming community. Participate in planting and harvesting with local farmers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium cooking class at Red Bridge Cooking School – boat transfer along the Thu Bon River to the school's riverside campus. Learn to prepare Hoi An's signature dishes: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac), Cao Lau noodles, and Hoi An-style pancakes (Banh Xeo).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise on the Thu Bon River on a traditional wooden sampan. Watch the Ancient Town's lanterns reflect on the river at dusk. Disembark at the riverside promenade for an evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel – request a Vietnamese breakfast spread with Pho, Xoi (sticky rice), and fresh tropical fruit.
meals.lunch: Lunch included in cooking class – enjoy the dishes prepared.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango Mango Restaurant (45 Nguyen Phuc Chu) – sophisticated fusion of Vietnamese and international cuisine with river views. Try the mango prawn salad and grilled black cod with ginger.

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle tour is best in the early morning before heat peaks. Bring sunscreen and a hat. Red Bridge cooking class includes a boat transfer – confirm departure time with the school.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to My Son Sanctuary – a UNESCO World Heritage Site of ancient Cham Hindu temples dating to the 4th–14th centuries. Private guided tour with an expert archaeologist. The site is most atmospheric in the early morning mist (depart by 7:30 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An. Visit premium tailoring shops on Le Loi Street – Hoi An is world-famous for bespoke tailoring. Have custom ao dai (Vietnamese tunic), suits, or dresses made within 24–48 hours. Recommended: Yaly Couture or A Dong Silk.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at An Bang Beach (8 km from Hoi An) – one of Vietnam's most beautiful and uncrowded beaches. Private beach club experience at Soul Kitchen or An Bang Beach Club with cocktails and fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before My Son departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Morning Glory Restaurant (106 Nguyen Thai Hoc) – founded by celebrated chef Trinh Diem Vy, serving authentic Hoi An street food in a refined setting. Must-try: Cao Lau and White Rose Dumplings.
meals.dinner: Dinner at An Bang Beach – fresh grilled seafood at a premium beachside restaurant. Choose from whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and catch-of-the-day fish with Vietnamese herbs and dipping sauces.

day_by_day.notes: My Son is approximately 40 km from Hoi An – arrange private driver for comfort. Tailoring orders placed today can be ready by Day 9 or Day 10 – confirm timeline with tailor.

day_by_day.morning: Morning flight from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) – approx. 1.5 hours, business class. Private luxury transfer to a premium hotel in District 1 (e.g., Park Hyatt Saigon, Caravelle Hotel, or Reverie Saigon). Check-in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided cultural tour of Saigon's colonial heritage: Visit the Reunification Palace (Dinh Thong Nhat), the stunning Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica (under renovation – exterior viewing), the Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel), and the Saigon Opera House. Stroll along Dong Khoi Street.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at Chill Sky Bar (AB Tower, 76 Le Lai) – one of Southeast Asia's highest rooftop bars with sweeping panoramic views of the Saigon skyline at night. Dress code: smart casual.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hoi An hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nha Hang Ngon (160 Pasteur, District 3) – a beloved Saigon institution set in a beautiful French colonial villa courtyard, serving street food from across Vietnam in a refined setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Deck Saigon (38A Nguyen U Di, Thao Dien, District 2) – a sophisticated riverside restaurant with stunning views of the Saigon River. Menu features premium Vietnamese and international dishes – try the pan-seared barramundi and beef tenderloin with lotus root.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. District 1 is Saigon's most walkable area – most afternoon sites are within walking distance or a short taxi ride. Book Chill Sky Bar in advance for weekend evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the War Remnants Museum (28 Vo Van Tan) – one of Vietnam's most powerful and moving museums, documenting the Vietnam War with striking photojournalism. A sobering but essential cultural experience. Afterward, visit the Ben Thanh Market for a curated premium shopping experience – lacquerware, conical hats, silk, and Vietnamese coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium spa and wellness afternoon at the hotel spa or a luxury day spa such as L'Apothiquaire Artisan Beaute (64 Truong Dinh, District 3) – indulge in a Vietnamese herbal body wrap, hot stone massage, and traditional facial. A restorative finale to 10 days of exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and final evening in Vietnam – celebrate the journey.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel – Vietnamese pho and banh mi station or full international buffet.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pho Hoa Pasteur (260C Pasteur St) – Saigon's most iconic pho restaurant, serving rich southern-style beef pho since 1960. A perfect final taste of Vietnamese street food culture.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Noir. Dining in the Dark (178/22 Co Giang, District 1) – a unique, world-renowned dining experience where guests eat in complete darkness served by visually impaired staff. A profoundly memorable and thought-provoking finale. Alternatively: Xu Restaurant Lounge (71 Hai Ba Trung) for a glamorous upscale Vietnamese tasting menu in a stunning Art Deco setting.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time for onward travel – arrange private airport transfer in advance. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Collect any tailored items from Hoi An that were shipped to the Saigon hotel. Tip guides and drivers generously – customary in Vietnam's premium tourism sector.
